t4540.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī, Abū Ṭarīf, a well-known Companion. He stood firm during the Riddah, was present at the conquests of Iraq and ʿAlī's wars, and died in 68 at age 120 (or 80).
as: A generous man, the son of a generous man. He had Companionship.
He accepted Islam and practised it well.
وكان عدي بن حاتم أحزم رأيا وأفضل في الإسلام رغبة ممن كان، فرق الصدقة في قومه
ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim was more resolute in judgment and more devoted to Islam than those around him. He distributed the alms among his people.
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, quoted by al-Mizzī
آمنت إذ كفروا، وعرفت إذ أنكروا، ووفيت إذ غدروا، وأقبلت إذ أدبروا
You believed when they disbelieved, recognized the truth when they denied it, remained faithful when they betrayed, and came forward when they turned back.
فلعمري إنا لنعرف حقه وفضله ورأي الخليفتين فيه وفي قومه
By my life, we recognize his due and his merit, and know what the two caliphs thought of him and his people.
عمر, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
آمنت إذ كفروا، وعرفت إذا أنكروا، ووفيت إذ غدروا، وأقبلت إذا أدبروا
You believed when they disbelieved, recognized the truth when they denied it, remained faithful when they betrayed, and came forward when they turned back.
وكان سيدا شريفا في قومه، خطيبا حاضر الجواب، فاضلا كريما
He was a respected leader among his people, an orator quick to answer, a man of merit and generosity.
سالم بن دارة الغطفاني, quoted by Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr
أبوك جواد ما يشق غباره ... وأنت جواد ليس تعذر بالعلل
Your father’s generosity could not be surpassed, and you are generous without making excuses.
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, quoted by Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr
آمنت إذ كفروا، وأقبلت إذ أدبروا، ووفيت إذ غدروا
You believed when they disbelieved, came forward when they turned back, and kept faith when they betrayed.
وكان جوادا شريفا في قومه، معظما عندهم وعند غيرهم، حاضر الجواب
He was generous, respected among his people and by others, and quick to answer.
أسلمت إذ كفروا، وعرفت إذ أنكروا، ووفيت إذ غدروا، وأقبلت إذ أدبروا
You accepted Islam when they disbelieved, recognized the truth when they denied it, kept faith when they betrayed, and came forward when they turned back.

t8276.bio: Ibn Ḥajar says Abū ʿImrān al-Anṣārī al-Shāmī, client of Umm al-Dardāʾ, was named Sulaymān or Sulaym ibn ʿAbd Allāh, truthful, of the fourth generation, and his report from the Prophet is mursal.

t850.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Thumāmah ibn Ḥazn al-Qushayrī al-Baṣrī, father of Abū al-Ward, as trustworthy, of the second generation, a mukhaḍram who came as a delegate to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb at age thirty-five.

t8562.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Ḥafṣa bint ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq as trustworthy and belonging to the third generation.

t8760.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Umm Kulthūm bint ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ al-Umawiyyah, who embraced Islam early, was a sister of ʿUthmān through his mother, a female Companion with hadiths, and died during ʿAlī's caliphate.

t928.bio: Ibn Ḥajar notes Jaʿdah ibn Hubayrah al-Ashjaʿī: al-Istīʿāb listed him separately from the preceding, while Ibn Abī Ḥātim combined them, which Ibn Ḥajar considers more likely.
